title: Trace + Fallbacks debugging walkthrough - VelocityCare
summary: Redwood SEs walked VelocityCare through the Console trace and request logs, demonstrated error analysis workflows, and discussed fallback routing and KV cache behavior. Key concerns: PII residency, latency SLOs for chat, and whether Dedicated or VPC Private is needed for audit controls.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-07 11:00 PT / Duration 52m / Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Micah Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (VelocityCare ML), Ethan Miles (VelocityCare SRE), Kara Nguyen (VM product), Salim Rahman (VelocityCare security)

Summary: quick demo of Console trace UI, then deep dive into a recent error pattern VelocityCare saw where fallback model returned hallucinated PII. Showed request inspector, playback, and KV cache TTL issues.

00:00:04 Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone thanks for carving time, can you see my screen? I have the Console up, we will walk through a real trace and then show the fallback routing behavior.
00:00:12 Priya Sharma: Yep we can see it, thanks Lena. quick context — we ran into a case where user support chat returned incorrectly formatted patient numbers and security flagged it.
00:00:30 Micah Patel: okay we'll pull the request trace, looking for the tokenization and prefix cache usage. sometimes the K V cache — it shows up as K V cash in the trace name — it can drop prefixes if the sequence length changes.
00:00:48 Ethan Miles: that was our suspicion, we saw spikes in latency when prefix cold start happened and then the fallback model was triggered which gave the worse output.
00:01:12 Jordan Reyes: i'll open the 'Request Inspector' panel, you should see the timeline: incoming request, model call to gpt-ish model, kvcache lookup, then fallback routing to smaller quantized model.
00:01:36 Kara Nguyen: can you point out which field shows the model selection?
00:01:40 Micah Patel: yep right here, the routing decision node — it logs policy name, latency thresholds, and why it decided to failover. for example: "policy: latency-window-200ms; reason: slot-saturated". sometimes the message is abbreviated in the export.
00:02:05 Priya Sharma: in our logs the model id is truncated, it showed like 'rw-v2-q4...' then later 'rw-v2-quant' and we couldn't map it back.
00:02:20 Micah Patel: that's a common transcription/labeling thing in the UI export; we also link to the model catalog entry. i'll show the mapping.
00:03:10 Micah Patel: (navigating) Playback mode is handy — you can replay the payload with the exact headers and see the runtime decisions. i'm going to force a playback with a 2s artificial delay to show fallback.
00:03:40 Ethan Miles: while you do that, quick question on data — if playback hits our logs, are we sending PII to Redwood hosted logs? we need to know retention and redaction.
00:03:58 Lena Ortiz: good question — for hosted customers our retention defaults 30 days but we have enterprise options: Dedicated capacity with audit log retention controls and Private (VPC) runs where you keep request logs in your S3 and we only store minimal telemetry in the control plane. also we support automatic PII redaction rules in the Console.
00:04:36 Salim Rahman: is that KMS integration for redaction keys? we need to be able to rotate keys via our HSM.
00:04:44 Jordan Reyes: yes, we integrate KMS/HSM; you can configure envelopes so raw payloads are encrypted before persisting. we also surface audit logs for key usage.
00:05:12 Micah Patel: replay triggered — you can see here: at 0.7s model A returned partial token stream then the router switched to model B. the KV cache entry was missing because the conversation context exceeded configured TTL.
00:05:40 Priya Sharma: TTL? we thought the cache was session-bound not time-based.
00:05:50 Micah Patel: it's both — by default we use session affinity plus time-to-live. if you have long conversations we recommend bumping the prefix cache TTL or using explicit session pinning. note that increasing TTL changes memory footprint and may affect eviction which is why we show a per-model memory metric.
00:06:20 Ethan Miles: got it — how do we detect cache evictions automatically? we found it hard to correlate evictions to latency spikes.
00:06:34 Jordan Reyes: Console exposes eviction events in the trace timeline and an alert rule you can pin to Slack. we can also export to your observability mix (datadog/newrelic).
00:06:50 Kara Nguyen: on the routing side, can we set priority so model B is only used as a last resort, not based on cost?
00:07:00 Micah Patel: yes policies are rule-based — you can order by latency targets, cost budget, or region. we recommend latency-first for user-facing chat, cost-first for background embedding jobs.
00:07:26 Priya Sharma: our SLO is 250ms p95 for chat — can Redwood meet that hosted? or do we need Dedicated?
00:07:36 Micah Patel: for p95 250ms it depends on model size and request length. with rw-v2-medium quantized we hit ~180–220ms p95 in our benchmarks for 512-token context on the hosted fleet in us-west-2, but sustained throughput at that latency often uses Dedicated pools to avoid noisy neighbors.
00:08:04 Ethan Miles: what's the ramp for Dedicated? if we commit to reserved capacity what's the lead time?
00:08:12 Lena Ortiz: typical lead time is 2–6 weeks depending on region and GPU type. we can provision burst capacity for pilots. we'll put the SLA and provisioning timelines in the follow-up.
00:08:36 Micah Patel: back to the trace — note the 'fallback reason' tag shows 'kv-miss + slot-saturated' and the payload shows presence of a sensitive token format. we also show a redaction suggestion: replace patterns that match your patient id regex before sending.
00:09:05 Salim Rahman: can the redaction be done client-side via SDK or do you prefer server-side?
00:09:16 Jordan Reyes: either — we provide helper transforms in SDKs, and server-side redaction in the gateway if you want enterprise policy enforcement. server-side is useful for centralized compliance.
00:09:45 Priya Sharma: i see in the trace an 'inflight-buff' warning — what does that mean?
00:09:52 Micah Patel: that's an internal shorthand — inflight buffer pressure. it means continuous batching queued more tokens than the configured soft-cap, which can increase tail latency. Reduce batching window or increase pool size.
00:10:20 Ethan Miles: our infra team is worried about costs when you recommend increasing pool size. how do we estimate cost impact?
00:10:30 Lena Ortiz: Optimize gives recommendations — it can run a cost/perf simulation for your workload and show token-level unit economics. we can attach a sample run to the pilot.
00:10:50 Kara Nguyen: can you show the error analysis flow when a transcript contains PII and we need to scrub and re-ingest?
00:11:02 Micah Patel: sure — open the 'Error Analysis' tab. here we have filters: model, route, error code, and a quick search for regex matches. we use a 'case pack' concept to bundle replay, logs, and affected prompts for handoff to ML.
00:11:30 Priya Sharma: that case pack would be helpful for our compliance review. can we automate case export to our ticketing system?
00:11:38 Jordan Reyes: yes — we support hooks to JIRA/ServiceNow and can push a sanitized payload automatically.
00:12:00 Micah Patel: (brief pause) i'm going to simulate a degraded node so you see automatic fallback to region-bypass and then model variant with lower memory.
00:12:25 Priya Sharma: watching — will that change the user-visible ID?
00:12:30 Micah Patel: no, it's transparent: request id stays the same and the trace shows both nodes. you can follow the request id across retries.
00:13:05 Ethan Miles: curious about tracing granularity — do we store full token logits or just meta events? for privacy and storage we prefer to avoid token-level retention.
00:13:20 Jordan Reyes: by default we store meta events and decoded outputs; token-level logits are optional and only for customers that enable full-fledged debugging. they're encrypted in transit and at rest.
00:13:46 Salim Rahman: we need SOC2 plus ISO27001 and proof of pen tests — do you have recent certs?
00:13:58 Lena Ortiz: yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001; i will share the compliance pack in the follow-up link. we also provide an architecture whitepaper for Private deployments.
00:14:20 Priya Sharma: thanks. another question: when fallback occurs can we label the segment as 'do-not-cache' to avoid reintroducing bad tokens into KV cache?
00:14:34 Micah Patel: good catch — yes you can add a 'do-not-cache' flag per route or tag response events on the fly. that will skip KV writes for that request id.
00:14:55 Kara Nguyen: is there a way to annotate traces with internal notes? our support team wants to leave contextual comments.
00:15:04 Jordan Reyes: there's an annotation pane; comments are time-stamped and we support linking to a playbook.
00:15:30 Micah Patel: moving on — i want to show the console trace exports; we'll export this case pack and you can open it locally. link: https://redwood.app/shared/casepack/velocicare-1126 (note: redacted link for demo).
00:15:50 Priya Sharma: we liked the 'model comparator' that shows outputs side-by-side — can we run that across rollouts?
00:16:02 Micah Patel: yes, compare function runs A/B output diffs and quality metrics against your eval set. we can attach your prompt suite to detect regressions.
00:16:20 Ethan Miles: ok let's talk timeline — we want a pilot with 50k monthly chat messages and SLOs at p95 250ms. we want to run a 4-week pilot and then consider Dedicated.
00:16:36 Lena Ortiz: understood. for pilot we usually provision a shared pool and set up alerting and telemetry exports. we'll also run Optimize's run to recommend quantization profiles.
00:16:54 Priya Sharma: do you support on-prem package? our compliance might push for air-gapped.
00:17:02 Lena Ortiz: yes, we have a Private deployment option that's customer-controlled and can be air-gapped; it's a different engagement and has longer lead time.
00:17:18 Salim Rahman: what about SAML and SCIM for SSO and automated user provisioning?
00:17:26 Jordan Reyes: supported — SAML/SSO plus SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC for role controls.
00:17:42 Micah Patel: quick note about a confusing label we sometimes see in traces — 'request playback: failed-transform' often caused by JSON-escaped characters in the client. we recommend normalizing payloads client-side.
00:18:10 Priya Sharma: we did see that; our serializer was adding stray backslashes.
00:18:20 Lena Ortiz: okay we'll capture that as an action item.
00:18:30 (fast forward)
00:28:00 Micah Patel: demo wrap-up — key places to instrument: request inspector, eviction alerts, fallback policies, and case-pack automated exports.
00:28:20 Priya Sharma: this answers many questions, thanks. a few nitpicks: we need clearer mapping between model ids and catalog entries in the CSV export and better labeling for quantized variants.
00:29:05 Jordan Reyes: we'll flag that UX item with product.
00:30:00 Lena Ortiz: time for the final Q&A — any blockers?
00:30:12 Ethan Miles: procurement needs estimated monthly cost for the pilot; can you provide a breakdown?
00:30:22 Lena Ortiz: yes we'll send a pilot quote with model cost, request logs addon, and optional Dedicated uplift.
00:31:00 Priya Sharma: also can you run a short benchmark of our sample workload to validate p95 numbers? we can upload a 24-hour sample trace.
00:31:12 Micah Patel: absolutely, we can run a head-to-head in our test harness. please share the CSV and we'll run Optimize for recommendations.
00:31:30 Kara Nguyen: can you include an explicit runbook for our SREs about triage steps when fallback occurs?
00:31:40 Jordan Reyes: yes we have a 'Fallback triage' playbook; we'll attach it.
00:32:05 Lena Ortiz: great — let's recap and list next steps.
00:32:15 (brief recap)
00:32:25 Lena Ortiz: recap: 1) Redwood to share compliance pack and SOC2/ISO docs; 2) SE to run a workload benchmark and Optimize run; 3) Pricing/pilot quote; 4) provide playbook and JIRA hook instructions; 5) UX note about model id mapping.
00:32:50 Priya Sharma: timeline: we'd like the benchmark within one week and quote within three days.
00:33:02 Lena Ortiz: sounds doable. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.
00:33:20 Salim Rahman: last ask — can we get an architecture diagram for Private deployment showing data flow and encryption points?
00:33:30 Jordan Reyes: yes we'll include that in the compliance pack.
00:34:00 (meeting winds down, casual chatter)
00:40:00 Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone, we'll send notes and next steps.
00:40:10 Priya Sharma: thanks all, appreciate it.

Transcript notes: some speaker attributions may be slightly off due to multi-party crosstalk. occasional transcription artefacts for acronyms (S A M L, K V cash) and model ids are abbreviated.
